title: One verb form for everyone
objective: Use the present tense, which always ends in -r and never changes with the person.
explanation: Good news: a Danish present-tense verb is the same for every person. Take the infinitive and add -r: “at spise” → “jeg spiser, du spiser, vi spiser”. “At være” (to be) becomes “er” and “at have” becomes “har”, again for everyone: “jeg er, de er”. You never need a table of endings.
sourceReference: Deepwater original starter course (2026-10-29), written for Echo; teacher review required before publishing.

exercises.feedbackCorrect: Right: “vi spiser”. Same form as “jeg spiser”.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Add -r to “spise”: “vi spiser”, the same as for jeg.

exercises.prompt: Complete: “Hun ___ i Aarhus.” (bor, at bo = to live)

exercises.feedbackIncorrect: “At være” is “er” in the present, for everyone.

exercises.prompt: Write three sentences about a normal day, each with a different verb in the -r form, for example “Jeg drikker kaffe.”
